hero_motto: FROM THE COMMUNITY FOR THE COMMUNITY
intro_p1: CONVOYRAMA is an independent HUB designed to provide high-level technical tools for the simulation community. Born from the need for a neutral space, we offer an integrated ecosystem where every driver and every VTC can find the resources they need to enhance their experience.
intro_p2: We are not a VTC; we are a community-driven HUB. If you have questions or want to collaborate, you can find dr.will on our central Discord server.
feature_pitstop_desc: Your quick technical stop for ATS and ETS2. Repair, refuel, and manage your cargo in seconds.
feature_lagdrive_desc: Direct mod synchronization. The fastest way to share files with your team.
feature_lagfm_desc: The official community radio. Enjoy the best music while you travel the routes.
feature_cardan_desc: P2P collectible cards from your VTC and the whole community. Draws, trading, and real foil. Available now.
feature_convoycast_desc: Events and convoys for ATS and ETS2, shared with the community.
feature_tuppertruck_desc: Do you like your truck? Pack it! Convert your current configuration into a mod ready for the dealership.
update_13_desc: PitStop 1.61.0 is now available to everyone with the HateU edition for Windows and Linux.
update_14_desc: TupperTruck 1.61.0 is now available for Windows and Linux, with updated support for ATS/ETS2 1.61.
update_0_desc: The first public version of Cardan is out — P2P collectible cards for real TruckersMP VTCs. Download the APK from the Cardan page.
update_1_desc: ConvoyCast is the new identity of the ATS and ETS2 events app.
update_2_desc: The repository is now public on GitHub, with native support for Windows and Linux.
update_3_desc: PitStop's first version built with Slint, compatible with ETS2 and ATS 1.60.
update_4_desc: The native TruckersMP launcher for Linux also opened its repository to the public.
update_5_title: The Discord Server Renamed to CONVOYRAMA
update_5_desc: The server, formerly LAG'S SPEED, is now called CONVOYRAMA to unify the identity and avoid confusion. It remains a memory chest for the old Canteras del Sur / Convoy Nocturno community, and now also serves as support for CONVOYRAMA as another channel.
update_6_desc: We're putting LAG-ID fully on hold to focus on shipping Cardan's release as soon as possible.
update_7_desc: We kicked off a series of humorous, AI-made music videos as a tribute to the community.
update_8_desc: The community's official radio app opened its repository to the public on GitHub.
update_9_desc: TupperTruck's first version ships, letting you pack your truck setup as a mod.
update_12_desc: The CONVOYRAMA project kicks off as a space for the TruckersMP community.
footer_tagline: If the mod explodes or your truck comes to life, we weren't here.
ps_desc: PitStop is an experimental save editor for ATS and ETS2. It modifies your save file directly to repair, refuel, and more. It's experimental — use it with care.
ps_note: Note: The application includes a small in-game overlay. Use Alt + 1 to refuel, repair, and remove cargo weight instantly on your last save. We recommend using F9 (quick save), pressing Alt + 1, and then F10 (load game).
ps_credits: Special thanks to Christian Mono from Convoy Nocturno for his invaluable help in testing and QA. And to Siberian Coffee from Los Andes Unidos for the inspiration and his tireless work for the community.
ps_f1_desc: Repair your truck and trailer to 100% without looking for a workshop.
ps_f2_desc: Fill the tank in seconds and forget about gas station stops.
ps_f3_desc: Remove the weight from your current cargo for a lighter drive.
ps_f4_desc: Works with both American Truck Simulator and Euro Truck Simulator 2.
ld_desc: The ultimate solution for direct mod sharing. Connect with other drivers and keep your files updated instantly.
ld_alpha_desc: LAGDrive is experimental and might fail, contain bugs, or leak your private photos... but since you spend all day on the road, we know you have no social life anyway, so there's nothing to worry about. Report bugs on CONVOYRAMA Discord.
ld_f1_desc: Direct transfer between players using P2P.
ld_f2_desc: Keep your entire team on the same version of mods.
ld_f4_desc: You decide which folders to share and when to sync.
fm_f1_desc: A tested and verified list of the best community radios, ready to play.
fm_f2_desc: Add your own streaming URLs and customize your tuner to your liking.
fm_f3_desc: Real-time view of today's TruckersMP events directly within the app.
fm_f4_desc: Available for Windows and Android, with a dedicated Web Player for iOS.
tt_tagline: "Pack your truck, buy it whenever you want"
tt_desc: Got a perfect truck, trailer, or car? With TupperTruck you can capture its exact configuration from your ATS or ETS2 1.61 save game and convert it into a Standalone Mod (.scs).
tt_alpha_desc: TupperTruck is experimental. Keep in mind that the tupper seal might not be 100% airtight: some accessories might not copy correctly. Use at your own risk.
tt_disclaimer: Note: We are not responsible if your truck becomes self-aware after packaging, if it tries to eat other trucks' mods, or if the dealership looks at you weird for trying to buy a truck you already had.
tt_f1_desc: Captures trucks, trailers, and cars with all their technical components directly from the save file.
tt_f2_desc: Generates an automatic .scs file for the official dealership.
tt_f3_desc: Do your friends want your exact same truck? Pass them the tupper and you're done.
tt_f4_desc: Works for both American Truck Simulator and Euro Truck Simulator 2.

dev_intro_p: Convoyrama tools don't just create visual images; they also embed structured metadata (JSON) within the generated PNG files. This allows Discord bots and other applications to read information directly from the image without OCR, supporting native UTF-8 (accents, emojis, and special characters).
dev_how_p: Data is stored in an auxiliary chunk of type iTXt (International Text) within the PNG structure. This format is the modern standard for international text and ensures the encoding is always UTF-8. We use specific keys (Keywords) to differentiate content types.

id_tagline: LEAVE YOUR MARK ON THE ROAD
id_desc: The road remembers every driver, but your identity defines the legacy. Take command of your journey and build your sovereign future within the simulation.
id_f1_desc: A unique profile that unifies your Steam and TruckersMP presence into a single simulation legacy.
id_f2_desc: Earn unique virtual currency and trade mods, items, or assets in a secure P2P market.
id_f3_desc: Professional administration tools: manage your team, assign ranks, and pay salaries automatically.
id_f4_desc: Central message board for announcements, recruitment, exclusive rewards, and a global P2P Market.
cardan_desc: Cardan turns every TruckersMP VTC into a real collectible card, drawn and traded peer-to-peer with your friends — no servers, no central accounts.
cardan_testing_note: Testing release. This is the first public version. It will have bugs. There is no backup for your collection — lose your phone or uninstall the app and your cards are gone forever (by design, not a bug). Trade cards to friends to keep them safe.
cardan_f1_desc: A new pack every 6 hours with 15 cards from ~14,500 real VTCs.
cardan_f3_desc: Swap up to 8 cards per side with friends. No servers.
cardan_f5_desc: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Carbon (extinct VTCs) and Diamond (crafted).
cardan_f6_desc: EN, ES, TR, DE, RU, PT, FR, ZH, JA, PL — the app speaks your language.
cardan_f7_desc: Visual effect that reacts when you tilt your phone.
cardan_f8_desc: Event editions: anniversary, Christmas, Halloween and more.
lt_desc: The native Linux launcher for TruckersMP. Manages the multiplayer engine and launches the game with one click.
lt_f1_desc: Select ETS2 or ATS and press PLAY. LAGTMP handles the rest.
lt_f2_desc: Downloads and maintains its own truckersmp-cli-lag instance automatically.
lt_f3_desc: Detects installed Proton and forces the Windows version of the game for compatibility.
lt_f4_desc: Full interface in English, Spanish, and Portuguese.
cc_desc: Organize, publish, and discover community events with ConvoyCast.

cc_f1_desc: Create and explore ATS and ETS2 events with dates, routes, details, and modes.
cc_f2_desc: Community events are shared directly between ConvoyCast clients.
cc_f3_desc: Profiles, votes, channels, and moderation lists for shared activity.
cc_f4_desc: ConvoyCast is designed to accompany your convoys on desktop and mobile.
ccp_intro: The CCPv1 (Convoyrama Convoy Protocol v1) is an independent CONVOYRAMA protocol for standardizing convoys, both on TruckersMP servers and outside of them. On TMP servers, TruckersMP's official rules always take priority over the CCPv1.
ccp_org_gloss: One or more drivers with authority over the convoy (chosen by the VTC or whoever hosts it). They may drive at the front, at the back, observe, or act as pilots. They set pace, formation, release, and incidents: their word is final.
ccp_desc_clasico: All participants leave together from the same point, follow the designated route, and arrive together at the destination. It's the base convoy mode.
ccp_desc_ciegas: The organization's members know the route in advance. The rest of the participants don't: they just have to follow the formation without knowing where they're headed until the convoy arrives.
ccp_desc_deriva: Not even the organization knows the route in advance: they improvise it on the go, turning wherever they happen to. Only the final destination is known.
ccp_desc_cruzado: Instead of a single departure point, several controlled departure points are designated in advance. It's not a case of everyone leaving from wherever they want: the points are fixed and agreed upon just like in the Classic mode, there's just more than one. This mode is mainly designed to make it easier for players who don't own certain map DLCs to take part: each group leaves from a point within the map they have available. The final stretch of the route is done together, all as a single convoy, to the destination. Up to the confluence point, each group rides as an independent convoy under the same rules; from there on, everyone forms a single convoy to the destination.
ccp_note_ciegas: None. Only who knows the route changes — the rest of the protocol stays the same.
ccp_note_deriva: None. Same as Blind Convoy, only how the route is defined changes — the rest of the protocol stays the same.
ccp_route_intro: This section provides guidance for planning the route; it does not add mandatory convoy rules.
ccp_route_1: DLC accessibility: when a route crosses maps with different DLC requirements, consider prioritizing, whenever practical, a destination or final leg on the base map or older, more accessible DLC. This allows people without the newest DLCs to join during the route and share the arrival, or at least take part in its final section.
ccp_route_2: Balance and variety: this does not mean excluding new DLCs or overlooking those who bought them. Routes should balance accessibility, map and scenery variety, recent content, and avoiding repeated routes. Do not base every convoy on the newest DLCs, but do not limit routes to older maps either.
ccp_route_3: Distance and route: the route should connect origin and destination in a reasonable, natural way. This also helps participants who use convoys to add kilometres to their VTC obtain a distance that represents the route.
ccp_route_4: Avoid artificial detours: a longer route is not always better. Unnecessary loops, curves added only to increase distance, or detours without real value can take more time and cause physically travelled distance to differ from what the game or VTC records. Prefer a route that is as direct as practical, attractive, and appropriately timed.
ccp_route_summary: The best route is not necessarily the newest, longest, or the one crossing the most DLCs: it is the one that balances accessibility, variety, duration, scenery, and value for participants.
ccp_cord_0: It applies to every convoy type, with no exceptions. Not every situation can be anticipated in a rulebook: when something unexpected happens, courtesy and good manners between drivers come first.
ccp_cord_1: If you're going to overtake, call it on the radio and ask permission before the maneuver.
ccp_cord_2: If you're being overtaken, leave plenty of room, ease off a bit to help the maneuver, and give the OK on the radio.
ccp_cord_3: If you have lag, or you see someone who does, call it on the radio so the group can react.
ccp_time_1: Depart punctually at the agreed time.
ccp_time_2: There should be a margin of 15 to 30 minutes between the meeting time and departure: the minimum gives time to gather the group; 30 is the maximum wait.
ccp_time_3: The convoy should last between one hour and an hour and a half from departure to the destination: neither too short nor too long. This is the same for every convoy type.
ccp_dep_1: The departure point must be reachable via direct quick travel. It shouldn't require driving long stretches just to get there.
ccp_marcha_1: Once the convoy departs, it does not stop, unless the organization says so or the incident protocol applies.
ccp_marcha_2: Maintain an adequate speed and predictable driving. Sudden braking is forbidden.
ccp_marcha_3: Know and respect traffic rules (signs and right of way) to avoid collisions and accidents. If the convoy has its own speed limit, it is set by the organization.
ccp_form_1: Slow or unstable vehicles (e.g.: double or triple trailers, special cargo) must go to the back of the convoy, so they don't hold up the group.
ccp_form_2: No large gaps between participants in the middle of the convoy: the group must advance as one, not left split in half.
ccp_form_3: If someone falls behind and leaves a gap, they must speed up and stick to the tail of the convoy.
ccp_form_4: If they don't, the drivers behind may overtake them to close the gap. If the gap becomes too large, that participant is no longer part of the convoy. The last vehicle must always stay stuck to the tail: no gap should be left, not even at the rear.
ccp_fuga_1: By default, no overtaking within the convoy: participants must stay together and hold formation; each VTC should make sure its players stay together.
ccp_fuga_2: Overtaking is only allowed in two cases: (1) organization's release, when the organization frees the convoy if it decides to — stop requiring formation speed and allow overtaking until the destination —; (2) gap closure, to close a large gap when someone has fallen behind and can't catch up (see Formation).
ccp_fuga_3: In both cases overtaking must be safe: no overtaking on curves, in dangerous areas, or in situations where an accident could be caused.
ccp_fuga_4: The driver being overtaken (or the slow vehicle) must slow down and allow the maneuver; they must not race once it has begun.
ccp_inc_1: If someone falls behind, disconnects, has an accident, or arrives late, the most common option is to rejoin at the end of the convoy. That avoids risky overtakes, doesn't break formation, and doesn't disturb the group. Other options (wait in a safe spot, keep going and catch up later, or any other agreed option) are defined in advance by the organization.
ccp_comm_1: Keep your mic muted when you're not speaking, to avoid background noise.
ccp_comm_2: Don't interrupt or use your mic/radio without a reason: the radio is for what the convoy needs, not for chatter, music, or annoying noises.
ccp_comm_3: During organizational moments (departure order, instructions, farewells) there should be radio silence except for what's strictly necessary, so you don't drown out the organization that is speaking.
ccp_cruz_time_1: Depart punctually at the agreed time from your point of origin.
ccp_cruz_time_2: Each meeting and departure point has its own time, calculated so that all groups reach the confluence point at the same time.
ccp_cruz_dep_1: Instead of a single point, several controlled departure points are designated in advance (never "everyone leaves from wherever they want"). This mode is mainly designed to make it easier for players who don't own certain map DLCs to take part.
ccp_cruz_dep_2: Each point must meet the same direct quick travel rule.
ccp_cruz_marcha_note: The rule applies to each individual leg up to the confluence point and, after that, to the convoy once merged on the final stretch.
ccp_cruz_form_note: The formation rules (no gaps, gap closure, and last vehicle stuck to the tail) apply from the confluence point onward, since that's when all groups become a single convoy to the destination.
